question: Let $X=\{1,2,3\}$ and let $P(X)$ denote the set of all subsets of $X$. A relation $R$ on $P(X)$ is defined by $ARB$ if $A\subseteq B$. Examine whether $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, and hence determine whether $R$ is an equivalence relation on $P(X)$.
explanation:
Reflexivity
For every $A\in P(X)$, every element of $A$ belongs to $A$. Hence, $$A\subseteq A$$ Therefore, $ARA$ for every $A\in P(X)$, and $R$ is reflexive.

Symmetry
For symmetry, $A\subseteq B$ must imply $B\subseteq A$. Consider $$A=\{1\},\qquad B=\{1,2\}$$ Then $$A\subseteq B$$ so $ARB$. However, $$B\nsubseteq A$$ because $2\in B$ but $2\notin A$. Hence, $BRA$ does not hold. Therefore, $R$ is not symmetric.

Transitivity
Suppose $ARB$ and $BRC$. Then $$A\subseteq B\quad\text{and}\quad B\subseteq C$$ Every element of $A$ is therefore an element of $B$, and every element of $B$ is an element of $C$. Hence, every element of $A$ belongs to $C$, giving $$A\subseteq C$$ Thus, $ARC$, so $R$ is transitive.

Final Result
The relation $R$ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric. Therefore, $R$ is not an equivalence relation on $P(X)$.

options.A: $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive; hence, it is not an equivalence relation.
options.B: $R$ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric; hence, it is not an equivalence relation.
options.C: $R$ is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive; hence, it is not an equivalence relation.
options.D: $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; hence, it is an equivalence relation.
